findings.reason: The protected Python solution implements a bidirectional BSTIterator over a BST's inorder traversal. It combines an explicit traversal stack for undiscovered nodes with a dynamically populated values list for cached entries. Moving next() retrieves from the cache if available or pops from stack and appends to cache; prev() decrements the cursor index over cached values. Construction and iterator calls take O(1) amortized time per operation and O(N) space; no candidate is required.

Lazy inorder stack traversal coupled with a cached values list allows bidirectional movement without duplicate tree node visits or lost states. index cursor accurately reflects current iterator location.

Each tree node is pushed/popped at most once, giving O(N + Q) total time for N nodes and Q operations (O(1) amortized per call). Auxiliary space is O(N) for values list and traversal stack. Complexity evidence is inherited and hash-bound.
Accepts BST root and operations trace, returning correct sequence of values and booleans for next, hasNext, prev, and hasPrev calls.

The approach accurately details stack-based lazy inorder traversal, discovered value caching, cursor index management for next/prev/hasNext/hasPrev, and O(1) amortized time / O(N) space bounds. Alternatives and edge cases cover eager inorder array construction, recomputing inorder per move overhead, root predecessor/successor search costs, first value boundary rules, direction reversal cache hits, traversal exhaustion, and skewed tree stack depth.
